row.scim_price_text: Enterprise: $250/mo billed annually (flat), shown as Contact sales on the plan card
row.evidence: Taskade's pricing page lists SCIM user provisioning only under Enterprise ("Everything in Max, plus"), and its SCIM via Okta guide says "This feature is only available under our Enterprise plan".
row.notes: New row. Flat workspace pricing, not per user: Free $0 (2 members), Pro $10/mo billed annually ($20 monthly, 10 users), Business $25/mo ($50 monthly, unlimited users, SAML SSO, API), Max $100/mo, Enterprise $250/mo billed annually ($500 monthly) per llms.txt and the pricing page's structured data, while the visible Enterprise card says Custom / Contact sales. SCIM needs SAML set up first and an organization created in Taskade; the SCIM token comes from the org overview page. Okta and Entra are set up as custom apps against https://www.taskade.com/scim/v2 (no catalogue app found). The Okta guide still says Taskade works exclusively with Okta, though an Entra guide exists. The SAML help article still names old plans (Ultimate/Unlimited). The public REST/Action APIs have no member-management endpoints.

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: Includes 'API and 100+ integrations' and SAML SSO; the API has no member-management endpoints.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.price_text: $250/mo billed annually ($500 monthly); plan card shows Custom / Contact sales

auth.token_source: Taskade organization overview page (SCIM token shown when the organization is created)

operations.notes: Okta guide enables Create Users, Update User Attributes, Deactivate Users and Push Groups; HTTP verbs are not documented.

attributes.notes: Only the unique identifier is documented; no attribute list is published.

roles.how: Pushed IdP groups are mapped in Taskade to workspace or folder access levels (Edit, Check or View; Editor, Viewer or Checker).

limitations.text: An organization must be created to group workspaces before groups can be provisioned; SAML must be configured first.
After a group member joins a folder, they must be removed from that folder manually.
The Okta guide says Taskade works exclusively with Okta, but a separate Azure AD SCIM guide exists.

scim.notes: Version 2.0 is inferred from the /scim/v2 base path; the help articles do not state a SCIM version.

capabilities.notes: By absence from the full OpenAPI specs; GET /projects/{projectId}/members lists a project's members only.

webhooks_user_events.notes: Webhook events cover projects, tasks and comments (e.g. project.joined, task.assigned); no workspace-member events.

rate_limits.text: 429 when exceeded; wait per X-Rate-Limit-Reset (no Retry-After header). Numeric limits not stated.

user_api.notes: Taskade has a public REST API v1 and Action API v2 (Business plan and up: 'API access'), but neither OpenAPI spec has endpoints to create, update, remove or deactivate workspace members; the only people endpoint reads project members. Recorded as no user-management API.

okta.notes: No OIN listing found (okta.com/integrations/taskade/ is 404); Taskade's guides use a custom 'Create App Integration' SAML app with SCIM enabled.

entra.notes: No Taskade entry in Microsoft Learn's SaaS app tutorial index; vendor guide configures automatic provisioning against the generic SCIM URL.

google.notes: A 'SAML via Google Workspace' help article exists (help-centre sitemap); not loaded. No provisioning documented.

conflicts.text: The visible Enterprise plan card says 'Custom' / 'Contact sales', while the same page's structured data and llms.txt give Enterprise at $250/month billed annually.
The SCIM via Okta guide says Taskade works exclusively with Okta, but a SCIM via Azure AD guide documents Entra provisioning.
The SAML via Okta article says SSO is on 'Ultimate and Enterprise plans' (older plan names); the pricing page puts SAML SSO on Business.

open_questions: Deprovisioning behaviour (deactivate vs remove, seat freed, sessions ended, data kept) is not documented.
No SCIM attribute list, filtering, pagination or rate limits are documented.
Whether SCIM DELETE is supported is not documented.
Whether SAML sign-in creates accounts just in time is not stated explicitly.
